# Scripts General Settings
```{r Setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Install necessary libraries
```{r Libraries}
#GENERAL BIOCONDUCTOR PACKAGES
    library(Biobase) #Standardized data structures to represent genomic data (ExpressionSet class)
    library(oligoClasses) #Classes for high-throughput arrays supported by oligo
     
#QUALITY CONTROL AND PRE-PROCESSING PACKAGES
    library(oligo) #To analyze oligonucleotide arrays (expression/SNP/tiling/exon) at probe-level. It supports Affymetrix (CEL files).
    library(arrayQualityMetrics) #To generate quality metrics reports for 1 and 2 color array microarray data in Bioconductor microarray data containers (ExpressionSet, NChannelSet, AffyBatch).
     
#ANALYSIS AND STATISTICS PACKAGES
    library(limma) #Data analysis, linear models and diff. expression for omics data.
    library(topGO) #For testing GOterms while accounting for the topology of the GO graph.
    library(clusterProfiler) #For functional characteristics of omics data. We use it for the KEGG analysis
     
#PLOTTING AND COLOR OPTIONS PACKAGES
    library(ggplot2) #Visualization package for various plots.
    library(ggrepel) #Provides geoms for ggplot2 to repel overlapping text labels.
    library(RColorBrewer) #To choose colors in heatmap and histograms.
    library(pheatmap) #For heatmap.

#FORMATTING/DOCUMENTATION PACKAGES
    library(dplyr) #Provides simple “verbs”-functions for data manipulation tasks.
    library(tidyr) #To create tidy data (col.=variab., row=osb., cell=value)
    library(tidytext) #To convert text data into a tidy format (word=row) for easier analysis and visualization of text data using other tidy tools like dplyr and ggplot2
#install.packages("tidytext")

#HELPERS
    library(stringr) #Data cleaning and preparation tasks
    library(AnnotationDbi) #For querying and manipulating SQLite-based annotation databases in Bioconductor
    library(ggpubr) #To create and customize publication-ready plots based on ggplot2.
    library(cowplot) #To combine plots into a single layout for publication-ready plots 
    library(patchwork) #To combine separate ggplots into the same graphic
```

# Install PD (platform design) Package for Salmo salar Array
As with every other library or package, we need to install this one
every time we are to run the analysis.
```{r PD package install}

# Install the package
install.packages("Path/To/Package", repos=NULL, type="source")

# Load the package
library(pd.s.salar1)
```

# Import of annotation data
Here we import the SDRF file to obtain our samples annotation.
We then convert the data from the file into an AnnotatedDataFrame,
which we will need later to create an ExpressionSet object.

We obtained the SDRF file by submitting our experimental data to ArrayExpress -
Functional Genomics Data collection from BioStudies by EMBL-EBI, via their
Annotare, their web-based submission tool for ArrayExpress.

For further processing of our data, we will use sample names, from the SDRF
"Array.Data.File" column, as row names.
```{r SDRF file}
# Load file
sdrf_location <- file.path("E-MTAB-15368.sdrf.txt")

# Import file
SDRF <- read.delim(sdrf_location)

# Assign row names 
rownames(SDRF) <- SDRF$Array.Data.File

# Create an AnnotatedDataFrame object
SDRF <- AnnotatedDataFrame(SDRF)
```

# Import of microarray expression data as "ExpressionSet"
Here we create an ExpressionSet object, which will contain
expression data (from the ".CEL" files), pheno data (from the SDRF file) and
the chip annotation package we specify.
```{r ExpressionSet object}

# Import files into an ExpressionSet object
raw_data <- oligo::read.celfiles(filenames = file.path("Path/To/CEL/Files",
                                                       SDRF$Array.Data.File),
                                    pkgname = "pd.s.salar1", verbose = FALSE, phenoData = SDRF)

# Check if the object is valid (e.g. sample names match between tables).
stopifnot(validObject(raw_data))

# View some of the lines of the raw data object
head(Biobase::pData(raw_data))
```

We can now select the columns containing relevant information for our analysis.
For example the ones with individuals identifiers and variables of interest.
```{r Subselect data}

# Select the relevant columns
Biobase::pData(raw_data) <- Biobase::pData(raw_data)[, c("Source.Name",
                                     "Characteristics.individual.",
                                     "Factor.Value.organism.part.",
                                     "Factor.Value.sampling.time.",
                                     "Factor.Value.developmental.stage.")]
```

# Quality Control of the raw and normalized data
In this section we look for outliers and how data clusters/behaves.
We use the expression intensity values, accessed with the "exprs" function.

We first visualize raw data and then repeat all plots with the normalized data.

## QC for raw data
Note: rows represent DNA locations on the chip and columns represent samples.
```{r QC: Expression intensity values}

# To see some of the rows and columns
Biobase::exprs(raw_data)[1:5, 1:5]
```

Since expression data is commonly analyzed on a logarithmic scale,
we calculate log2, and we then perform and plot a PCA.

This particular code was used for the analysis of the ES group data.
Here the color indicates the maturation stage (early mature/immature) and the
shape indicates the sampling time (T0, T1 or T2), which are 2 of our 3
variables of interest, being tissue/organism part our 3rd variable of interest.
```{r QC: PCA of raw data}

# Logaritmic scale
exp_raw <- log2(Biobase::exprs(raw_data))

# Perform the PCA
PCA_raw <- prcomp(t(exp_raw), scale. = FALSE)

# Calculate variance
percentVar <- round(100*PCA_raw$sdev^2/sum(PCA_raw$sdev^2),1)

# Calculate standard deviation
sd_ratio <- sqrt(percentVar[2] / percentVar[1])

# Prepare data frame for PCA plot
dataGG <- data.frame(PC1 = PCA_raw$x[,1], PC2 = PCA_raw$x[,2],
                    SamplingTime = pData(raw_data)$Factor.Value.sampling.time.,
                    MaturationStage = pData(raw_data)$Factor.Value.developmental.stage.,
                    OrganismPart = pData(raw_data)$Factor.Value.organism.part.)

# PCA plot
RawPlot <- ggplot(dataGG, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = SamplingTime, colour = MaturationStage)) +
  facet_wrap(~ OrganismPart, ncol = 1, dir = "v") +
  ggtitle("PCA plot of the log-transformed raw expression data") +
  xlab(paste0("PC1, VarExp: ", percentVar[1], "%")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2, VarExp: ", percentVar[2], "%")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))+
  coord_fixed(ratio = sd_ratio) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4,7,15)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange2", "dodgerblue4"))
RawPlot

ggsave("RawPCA.tiff",units="in", width=6, height=4, dpi=300)

```


Here we visualize the raw data probe intensities via a boxplot graph,
where each box represents and individual microarray or sample.

The "oligo::boxplot" function accesses the expression data and performs a
log2-transformation by default.

A not homogeneous distribution of probe intensities from all arrays/samples
is an indicative that a normalization process is required.
```{r QC: Boxplot of raw probe intensities}

oligo::boxplot(raw_data,
               main = "Boxplot of log2-intensitites for the raw data")

```


Relative Log Expression (RLE) plots are part of the QC procedure where we can
have a general view of the expression of all samples and identify variations.

We first perform background adjustment and summarization, without
the normalization step.

Since the output data of the RMA function is in log2 scale by default, we do not
need to further apply log2 manually.
```{r QC: RMA without normalization}

palmieri_eset <- oligo::rma(raw_data, normalize = FALSE)

```

We then calculate the medians of the expression values, we use rows since, in
the ExpressionSet object the transcripts are represented by rows and the
single microarrays by columns.
```{r QC: RLE without normalization}

# Calculate transcripts (rows) medians
row_medians_assayData <- 
  Biobase::rowMedians(as.matrix(Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset)))

# Substract transcript median intensity
RLE_data <- sweep(Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset), 1, row_medians_assayData)

# Create data frame
RLE_data <- as.data.frame(RLE_data)

RLE_data_gathered <- 
  tidyr::gather(RLE_data, sample_array, log2_expression_deviation)

# Create a new column with row names
dataGG$sample_array <- rownames(dataGG)

# Move the recently created column to the first column
dataGG <- dataGG[, c(ncol(dataGG), 1:(ncol(dataGG)-1))]

# Merge data frames
RLE_data_gathered <- merge(dataGG, RLE_data_gathered, by = "sample_array", all = TRUE)

# To remove the two PCA columns, change number according to columns position
RLE_data_gathered <- RLE_data_gathered[ , -2]

# Boxplot
ggplot2::ggplot(RLE_data_gathered, aes(sample_array,
                                       log2_expression_deviation)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, aes(colour = MaturationStage, fill = SamplingTime)) +
  facet_wrap(~ OrganismPart, ncol = 1, dir = "v") +
  ylim(c(-2, 2)) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "aquamarine4", 
                                  angle = 60, size = 6.5, hjust = 1 ,
                                  face = "bold"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "burlywood" , "cornflowerblue"))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange4", "darkblue"))

ggsave("RLEplot.tiff",units="in", width=10, height=8, dpi=300)

```

## QC for normalized data
Here we apply the full RMA algorithm to perform background adjustment,
normalization and summarization of our data.
```{r QC: RMA with normalization}

palmieri_eset_norm <- oligo::rma(raw_data, normalize=TRUE)

```

Once normalization is done, we can repeat some of the QC analysis and plots
obtained for the raw data to compare and assess quality of the normalized data.

Again, this code was used for the analysis of the ES group data, and so the
color indicates the maturation stage (early mature/immature) and the
shape indicates the sampling time (T0, T1 or T2), which are 2 of our 3
variables of interest, being tissue/organism part our 3rd variable of interest.
```{r QC: PCA of normalized data}

# Extract expression values
exp_palmieri <- Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset_norm)

# Perform the PCA
PCA <- prcomp(t(exp_palmieri), scale = FALSE)

# Calculate variance
percentVar <- round(100*PCA$sdev^2/sum(PCA$sdev^2),1)

# Calculate standard deviation
sd_ratio <- sqrt(percentVar[2] / percentVar[1])

# Prepare data frame for PCA plot
dataGG <- data.frame(PC1 = PCA$x[,1], PC2 = PCA$x[,2],
                    SamplingTime = 
                     Biobase::pData(palmieri_eset_norm)$Factor.Value.sampling.time.,
                    MaturationStage = 
                     Biobase::pData(palmieri_eset_norm)$Factor.Value.developmental.stage.,
                    OrganismPart = 
                     Biobase::pData(palmieri_eset_norm)$Factor.Value.organism.part.)


RMAPlot <- ggplot(dataGG, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = SamplingTime, colour = MaturationStage)) +
  facet_wrap(~ OrganismPart, ncol = 1, dir = "v") +
  ggtitle("PCA plot of the calibrated, summarized data") +
  xlab(paste0("PC1, VarExp: ", percentVar[1], "%")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2, VarExp: ", percentVar[2], "%")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = sd_ratio) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4,7,15)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange2", "dodgerblue4"))
RMAPlot

ggsave("RMA_PCA.tiff",units="in", width=6, height=4, dpi=300)

```

Here we repeat the intensities boxplot with the normalized data to verify that
now all boxes show an even intensity distribution.
```{r QC: Boxplot of normalized probe intensities}

oligo::boxplot(palmieri_eset_norm, 
               main = "Boxplot of log2-intensitites for the normalized data")
```

Here we repeat the RLE plot with the normalized data to verify that
now all boxes show an even intensity distribution.
```{r QC: RLE with normalization}

# Calculate transcripts (rows) medians
row_mediansNorm_assayData <- 
  Biobase::rowMedians(as.matrix(Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset_norm)))

# Substract transcript median intensity
RLEnorm_data <- sweep(Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset_norm), 1, row_mediansNorm_assayData)

# Create data frame
RLEnorm_data <- as.data.frame(RLEnorm_data)

RLEnorm_data_gathered <- 
  tidyr::gather(RLEnorm_data, sample_array, log2_expression_deviation)

# Create a new column with row names
dataGG$sample_array <- rownames(dataGG)

# Move the recently created column to the first column
dataGG <- dataGG[, c(ncol(dataGG), 1:(ncol(dataGG)-1))]

# Merge data frames
RLEnorm_data_gathered <- merge(dataGG, RLEnorm_data_gathered, by = "sample_array", all = TRUE)

# To remove the two PCA columns, change number according to columns position
RLEnorm_data_gathered <- RLEnorm_data_gathered[ , -2]

# Boxplot
ggplot2::ggplot(RLEnorm_data_gathered, aes(sample_array,
                                       log2_expression_deviation)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, aes(colour = MaturationStage, fill = SamplingTime)) +
  facet_wrap(~ OrganismPart, ncol = 1, dir = "v") +
  ylim(c(-2, 2)) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "aquamarine4", 
                                  angle = 60, size = 6.5, hjust = 1 ,
                                  face = "bold"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "burlywood" , "cornflowerblue"))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkorange4", "darkblue"))

ggsave("RLEplotNorm.tiff",units="in", width=10, height=8, dpi=300)

```

Once we corroborate that all samples are normalized we perform a heatmap
clustering analysis with the sample-to-sample distances, where sample names
are row-names, to see how well samples cluster regarding our study variables.
```{r QC: Heatmap of normalized data}

# Get distances
dists <- as.matrix(dist(t(exp_palmieri), method = "manhattan"))

# Use row names
rownames(dists) <- row.names(pData(palmieri_eset_norm))

# Choose color palette
hmcol <- rev(colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "YlOrRd"))(255))
colnames(dists) <- NULL
diag(dists) <- NA

# Set annotation data
annotation_for_heatmapALL <- data.frame(dataGG$SamplingTime, dataGG$MaturationStage, dataGG$OrganismPart)
row.names(annotation_for_heatmapALL) <- row.names(pData(palmieri_eset_norm))

# Colors for annotation data
ann_colors <- list(
    SamplingTime = c("blue4","darkcyan","cadetblue3"),
    MaturationStage = c("darksalmon","darkolivegreen3"),
    OrganismPart = c("burlywood","white", "azure3"))

# Plot heatmap
png("HeatmapRMA.png", width = 4000, height = 4000, res = 300)
pheatmap(dists, col = (hmcol), 
         annotation_row = annotation_for_heatmap,
         annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         legend = TRUE, 
         treeheight_row = 0,
         legend_breaks = c(min(dists, na.rm = TRUE), 
                         max(dists, na.rm = TRUE)), 
         legend_labels = (c("small distance", "large distance")),
         main = "Clustering heatmap for the calibrated samples")
dev.off()

# Optional: Generate individual heatmaps by OrganismPart
parts <- unique(as.character(annotation_for_heatmapALL$OrganismPart))
parts <- parts[!is.na(parts)]  # drop NA parts

for (part in parts) {
    
     # samples belonging to this OrganismPart
    subset_samples <- rownames(annotation_for_heatmapALL)[annotation_for_heatmapALL$OrganismPart == part]
    
    # intersect with dists rownames in case some names are missing / mismatched
    subset_samples_in_dists <- intersect(subset_samples, rownames(dists))
    
      if (length(subset_samples_in_dists) == 0) {
    message("Skipping '", part, "': no matching samples found in distance matrix.")
    next
  }

  if (length(subset_samples_in_dists) < 2) {
    message("Skipping '", part, "': only ", length(subset_samples_in_dists), " sample(s) — need >=2 to plot a heatmap.")
    next
  }
    
    sub_dists <- dists[subset_samples_in_dists, subset_samples_in_dists, drop = FALSE]
    sub_annotation <- annotation_for_heatmapALL[subset_samples_in_dists, , drop = FALSE]
    
    # sanitize filename (remove/replace spaces and problematic chars)
  safe_part <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_\\-]", "_", part)
  file_name <- paste0("Heatmap_", safe_part, ".png")

    # plot
    png(file_name, width = 4000, height = 4000, res = 300)
    pheatmap(sub_dists,
        col = hmcol,
        annotation_row = sub_annotation,
        annotation_colors = ann_colors,
        legend = TRUE,
        treeheight_row = 0,
        legend_breaks = c(min(sub_dists, na.rm = TRUE), max(sub_dists, na.rm = TRUE)),
        legend_labels = c("small distance", "large distance"),
        main = paste("Clustering heatmap -", part)
    )
    dev.off()
    
    message("Saved heatmap for: ", part)
}
```


Since microarray data can have probes with low intensity and low variance
across arrays, these could be wrongly detected as differentially expressed,
so here we produce a histogram based on median probe intensities to visualize
their distribution, and check if a filtering based on intensity is needed.

Our histogram showed we can see a normal distribution, so we 
decide NOT to proceed with any filtering since it doesn't seem necessary.
```{r QC: Intensity histogram}

palmieri_medians <- rowMedians(Biobase::exprs(palmieri_eset_norm))

hist_res <- hist(palmieri_medians, 100, col = "cornsilk1", freq = FALSE, 
            main = "Histogram of the median intensities", 
            border = "antiquewhite4",
            xlab = "Median intensities")
```

## Match Probe-To-Gene DB with Expression Data
Here we encountered a difficulty when running the "select()" function
from AnnotationDbi to add annotation information to our ExpressionSet object,
we got an error indicating that there was no "c.probes" table found, so we
proceeded as described in "Annotation of TC: TC-To-Expression - "c.probes" view"
and create a view of our "probes" table, with the expected name "c.probes", to
work around the issue and be able to properly use the "select()" function.

Once this view is created and copied to the SQL in our package, when loading
again the package we just need to list the tables to verify "c.probes" is there
as it should. If there is no "c.probes" verify if the backup copy exists, if it
does run from step 8, since you already have the EDIT SQL file with "c.probes",
if the backup copy is not there, then run from step 7.

```{r Annotation of TC: TC-To-Expression - "c.probes" view}
#  file.path(pkg_path, "salmontranscriptclusterbak.sqlite"),
#  overwrite = TRUE)

# 8. Copy the contents of the edited DB into the installed file (the edited file is in the working folder so you can edit the name directly there to avoid confusions)
#file.copy(
#  "salmontranscriptclusterEDIT.sqlite",
#  file.path(pkg_path, "salmontranscriptcluster.sqlite"),
#  overwrite = TRUE)

# 9. Restart R (to unload any cached DB connections) to check if AnnotationDbi
#sees the new table
#library(salmontranscriptcluster.db)
#library(AnnotationDbi)
con <- AnnotationDbi::dbconn(salmontranscriptcluster.db)
DBI::dbListTables(con)
```


Once we are sure that our transcript cluster DB (TC DB) has the "c.probes" view,
we can proceed to add annotation information from our transcript cluster DB to
our ExpressionSet object which to this point contains all the probes in the ADF
plus the array control probes. We do this step by linking the PROBEIDs from our
ExpressionSet object to our TC DB so that here the TC DB can look them up
through their ENTREZID to retrieve their associated gene symbols and gene names
via the OrgDB we associated in our TC DB, which stores this information.
```{r Annotation of TC: TC-To-Expression - Add annotation info}
# 10. Use the select() function.
anno_palmieri <- AnnotationDbi::select(salmontranscriptcluster.db,
                                  keys = (featureNames(palmieri_eset_norm)),
                                  columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENENAME"),
                                  keytype = "PROBEID")

write.csv(anno_palmieri, "ProbeToSymbol.csv", row.names = FALSE)

anno_palmieri <- subset(anno_palmieri, !is.na(SYMBOL))
write.csv(anno_palmieri, "ProbeToSymbolnotNA.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 11. Removing multiple mappings
# 11.1. Group anno_palmieri by PROBEID so subsequent operations can work
#separately on each probe group (each PROBEID).
#This does not change how we see the object structure.
anno_grouped <- group_by(anno_palmieri, PROBEID)

# 11.2. Sum groups and indicate the number of different genes assigned to a transcript cluster in the column no_of_matches
anno_summarized <- 
  dplyr::summarize(anno_grouped, no_of_matches = n_distinct(SYMBOL))
head(anno_summarized)

# To filter probes that map to more than 1 probe; dim(probe_stats) prints the result
anno_filtered <- filter(anno_summarized, no_of_matches > 1)
head(anno_filtered)

probe_stats <- anno_filtered 
nrow(probe_stats)

# 11.3. We want to remove probe IDs that match the ones in probe_stats, as those have multiple mappings, and it will be difficult to know which mapping is “correct”.
#We assign these IDs to the variable ids_to_exclude
ids_to_exlude <- (featureNames(palmieri_eset_norm) %in% probe_stats$PROBEID)
table(ids_to_exlude)

#We remove the duplicated probes from the ExpressionSet object 
palmieri_final <- subset(palmieri_eset_norm, !ids_to_exlude)
validObject(palmieri_final)

# As we excluded probe IDs from the assay data, we have to also exclude them from the feature data anno_palmieri

# fData enables us to access the feature data of an ExpressionSet object
# We generate a PROBEID column in fData(palmieri_final) and assign the original row names of fData(palmieri_final) to it
fData(palmieri_final)$PROBEID <- rownames(fData(palmieri_final))

# We left-join with anno_palmieri, which already contains “SYMBOL” and “GENENAME”. This keeps the rows and columns of the first object and adds the corresponding column entries of the second object. By doing so, we thus add the “SYMBOL” and “GENENAME” columns from anno_palmieri for only the PROBEIDs that are in fData(palmieri_final) and thus get the feature Data for the filtered probes with unique mapping.
fData(palmieri_final) <- left_join(fData(palmieri_final), anno_palmieri)

# Make sure PROBEIDs are rownames in the resulting palmieri_final object
rownames(fData(palmieri_final)) <- fData(palmieri_final)$PROBEID 
validObject(palmieri_final)
```


# Differential Gene Expression (DGE) Analysis
To determine which genes are differentially expressed in our groups we fit a 
linear model to our expression data.

We first defined our experimental variables, which in the ES group data are
sampling times, maturation stages and tissues. Then, to better understand how
to apply the LM to our data we took a look at the "limma" package user guide,
and determined that the "9.7 Multi-Level Experiments" was the option that best
suited our data.

So then, here, we introduce the abbreviations
“G”, “L” and “B” for the tissues, since we will create a model per tissue, and
this will help to filter information, later on we use “EM” and “IM” for the
maturation stages and “T0”, “T1” and “T2” for the sampling times.
```{r DGE-A: Tissue abbreviation for Linear Models}
# Extract tissue/organism part data and add abbreviations 
tissue <- str_replace_all(Biobase::pData(palmieri_final)$Factor.Value.organism.part.,
                  " ", "_")
tissue <- case_when(tissue == "gonad" ~ "G",
                           tissue == "liver" ~ "L",
                           tissue == "brain" ~ "B")
```

Since in our data the individual/fish is duplicated in tissue, because we have
3 tissues from the same fish, but not in maturation stage or in sampling time,
because each fish had only 1 maturation stage and was sampled only in 1 of the 3
sampling times, we concluded it would be less troubled if we separated tissue
and created 3 models in total, 1 per tissue. Where all comparisons, which would
include sampling time and maturation stage would be considered when using the
"makeContrasts" function. This way it was also not necessary to use the blocking
and correlation functions for the individuals in the fitted models, since we
don't need to make comparisons within the same individual, only between them.

In the linear models, the "~0" argument creates the model without an intercept,
so all comparisons can be later specified with the "makeContrasts" function, and
differentially expressed genes can be obtained specifically for each comparison
with the "topTable" function.

## Gonad Linear Model
Here we filter expression data from the ExpressionSet object to only work with
the expression data from all the gonad samples.
```{r DGE-A: Linear Model for Gonad}

# Filter gonad samples for all sampling times and maturation stages.
keep_g <- tissue == "G"
expr_g <- palmieri_final[, keep_g]
meta_g <- pData(palmieri_final)[keep_g, ]

# Verify if we have the same number of columns and rows.
ncol(expr_g)
nrow(meta_g)
all(colnames(expr_g) == rownames(meta_g))  # should be TRUE if names exist

# Create a column with our 2 remaining variables combined
meta_g$group <- factor(paste(meta_g$Factor.Value.sampling.time., meta_g$Factor.Value.developmental.stage., sep="."))

# Design matrix for Gonad samples
design_g <- model.matrix(~0 + group, data = meta_g)

# Define column and row names
colnames(design_g) <- levels(meta_g$group)
rownames(design_g) <- meta_g$Characteristics.individual.
head(design_g[,])

# Introduce abbreviations for maturation stages
colnames(design_g) <- gsub("Early mature", "EM", colnames(design_g))
colnames(design_g) <- gsub("Immature", "IM", colnames(design_g))
colnames(design_g)

# Determine & rank how many columns are linearly independent (we need all to be)
qr(design_g)$rank
ncol(design_g) # Verify column number

# Linear model fit
fit_g <- lmFit(expr_g, design_g)

# Define contrast matrix
contrasts_g <- makeContrasts(
  G_T0vsT1_IM = T0.IM - T1.IM,
  G_T0vsT1_EM = T0.IM - T1.EM,
  G_T0vsT2_IM = T0.IM - T2.IM,
  G_T0vsT2_EM = T0.IM - T2.EM,
  G_T1_IMvsEM = T1.IM - T1.EM,
  G_T1vsT2_IM = T1.IM - T2.IM,
  G_T1IMvsT2EM = T1.IM - T2.EM,
  G_T1EMvsT2IM = T1.EM - T2.IM,
  G_T1vsT2_EM = T1.EM - T2.EM,
  G_T2_IMvsEM = T2.IM - T2.EM,
  levels = design_g
)

# Fit linear model with contrast matrix
fit_g2 <- contrasts.fit(fit_g, contrasts_g)

# Apply empirical Bayes variance smoothing to the standard errors
fit_g2 <- eBayes(fit_g2)

# Obtain differentially expressed genes for each comparison
table_g1 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T0vsT1_IM", number = Inf)
table_g2 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T0vsT1_EM", number = Inf)
table_g3 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T0vsT2_IM", number = Inf)
table_g4 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T0vsT2_EM", number = Inf)
table_g5 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T1_IMvsEM", number = Inf)
table_g6 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T1vsT2_IM", number = Inf)
table_g7 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T1IMvsT2EM", number = Inf)
table_g8 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T1EMvsT2IM", number = Inf)
table_g9 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T1vsT2_EM", number = Inf)
table_g10 <- topTable(fit_g2, coef="G_T2_IMvsEM", number = Inf)

# Explore data
head(table_g1)
head(table_g2)

# To get number of DE genes per comparison
sum(table_g1$adj.P.Val < 0.05)

# Check p-value distributions: Enriched near 0 → strong DE
hist(table_g1$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T0vsT1_IM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g2$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T0vsT1_EM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g3$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T0vsT2_IM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g4$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T0vsT2_EM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g5$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T1_IMvsEM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g6$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T1vsT2_IM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g7$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T1IMvsT2EM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g8$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T1EMvsT2IM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g9$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T1vsT2_EM", xlab = "p-values")
hist(table_g10$P.Value, col = brewer.pal(3, name = "Set2")[1],
     main = "G_T2_IMvsEM", xlab = "p-values")

```

## Expression Bias Test
Here we perform a brief check up of our data to verify which set of genes is
best to use as background for our DGE analysis.
Since the check up starts with one table from one tissue, we can repeat it for
every table of every tissue, or at least some tables from all 3 tissues.

In our case our test results suggested using tissue-specific backgrounds.
```{r DGE-A: Expression Bias Test}

# Define UP and DOWN gene sets (you may change the comparison being tested)
G_UP_genes   <- rownames(table_b10)[table_b10$logFC >=  2 & table_b10$adj.P.Val < 0.05]
G_DOWN_genes <- rownames(table_b10)[table_b10$logFC <= -2 & table_b10$adj.P.Val < 0.05]

# Combine UP and DOWN genes for total DE genes
de_genes <- c(G_UP_genes, G_DOWN_genes)
de_genes <- de_genes[de_genes %in% rownames(expr_b)]  #Ensure DEG exist in expression object

# To extract expression data as matrix
if(class(expr_b) == "ExpressionSet") {
  expr_b_matrix <- exprs(expr_b)  #This extracts the actual data
} else {
  expr_b_matrix <- expr_b  #Already a matrix
}

# Get expression means per probe
all_avg_expr <- rowMeans(expr_b_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)

# Get expression for DEG
de_avg_expr <- all_avg_expr[de_genes]

# Get expression for non-DE genes (background)
bg_genes <- setdiff(rownames(expr_b), de_genes)
bg_avg_expr <- all_avg_expr[bg_genes]


# Perform a statistical test and print results
# Wilcoxon rank-sum test (non-parametric) where:
# H0: DE genes and background have same expression distribution
# H1: DE genes have HIGHER expression (one-sided)
test_result <- wilcox.test(de_avg_expr, bg_avg_expr, alternative = "greater")

cat("\n========== EXPRESSION BIAS TEST RESULTS ==========\n")
cat("DE genes median expression:", round(median(de_avg_expr), 3), "\n")
cat("Background median expression:", round(median(bg_avg_expr), 3), "\n")
cat("Fold difference (DE/BG):", round(median(de_avg_expr)/median(bg_avg_expr), 2), "x\n")
cat("Wilcoxon p-value:", format(test_result$p.value, digits=3, scientific=TRUE), "\n")


# Print interpretation of the test results
fold_diff <- median(de_avg_expr)/median(bg_avg_expr)

if(fold_diff > 2 && test_result$p.value < 0.001) {
  cat("\n>>> STRONG BIAS DETECTED <<<\n")
  cat("RECOMMENDATION: Use expression-matched background (genefinder)\n")
  recommendation <- "matched"
} else if(fold_diff > 1.5 && test_result$p.value < 0.01) {
  cat("\n>>> MODERATE BIAS DETECTED <<<\n")
  cat("RECOMMENDATION: Consider expression-matched background\n")
  recommendation <- "maybe_matched"
} else {
  cat("\n>>> NO SIGNIFICANT BIAS <<<\n")
  cat("RECOMMENDATION: Tissue-specific background is sufficient\n")
  recommendation <- "tissue_only"
}


#This is an example of the results we got for our data
#DE genes median expression: 6.706 
#Background median expression: 6.024 
#Fold difference (DE/BG): 1.11 x
#Wilcoxon p-value: 1.6e-121
#>>> NO SIGNIFICANT BIAS <<<
#RECOMMENDATION: Tissue-specific background is sufficient
```

## Create Tissue-Specific Backgrounds
Here we create the 3 tissue-specific backgrounds we will need for our analysis.
```{r DGE-A: Tissue-Specific Backgrounds}

# Function to create background
create_tissue_bg <- function(expr_set, annotation_db = salmontranscriptcluster.db) {

  # Extract expression data
  expr_matrix <- exprs(expr_set)
  
  # Average expression across samples
  avg_expr <- rowMeans(expr_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Threshold: median expression (genes "present" in tissue)
  threshold <- median(avg_expr, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Select expressed probes
  expressed_probes <- rownames(expr_matrix)[avg_expr > threshold]
  
  # Intersect with valid annotated probes
  valid_probes <- keys(annotation_db, keytype = "PROBEID")
  background_probes <- intersect(expressed_probes, valid_probes)
  
  # Map to ENTREZ
  bg_entrez <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    annotation_db,
    keys = background_probes,
    keytype = "PROBEID",
    columns = "ENTREZID"
  )
  
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  bg_entrez <- unique(na.omit(bg_entrez$ENTREZID))
  
  cat("Background created:\n")
  cat("  Expressed probes:", length(expressed_probes), "\n")
  cat("  With annotation:", length(background_probes), "\n")
  cat("  Unique ENTREZ IDs:", length(bg_entrez), "\n")
  
  return(list(
    probes = background_probes,
    entrez = bg_entrez,
    threshold = threshold
  ))
}

# Create your 3 backgrounds
brain_bg <- create_tissue_bg(expr_b)
gonad_bg <- create_tissue_bg(expr_g)
liver_bg <- create_tissue_bg(expr_l)

# Check overlap between tissues
# If you see high overlap (>90%), the tissues are very similar.
# If you see moderate overlap (60-80%), that's somewhat expected tissue specificity.
cat("Brain vs Gonad shared probes:", length(intersect(brain_bg$probes, gonad_bg$probes)), "\n")
cat("Brain unique probes:", length(setdiff(brain_bg$probes, gonad_bg$probes)), "\n")
cat("Gonad unique probes:", length(setdiff(gonad_bg$probes, brain_bg$probes)), "\n")

# Save all three
save(brain_bg, gonad_bg, liver_bg, file = "tissue_backgrounds_27mar.RData")

# Verify loading works
rm(brain_bg, gonad_bg, liver_bg)
load("tissue_backgrounds_27mar.RData")
ls()

# Check mapping detail for one tissue
test_map <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  salmontranscriptcluster.db,
  keys = brain_bg$probes[1:100],  # First 100 probes
  keytype = "PROBEID",
  columns = "ENTREZID"
)

# See if any probes map to multiple ENTREZ IDs
table(table(test_map$PROBEID))
```

From this point forward we have duplicated chunks for the same step or analysis,
because the first chunk has the code to process a single comparison, whereas the
second chunk will have the code to process all the comparisons we have. This was
useful while preparing the script, since we could use the single comparison code
to see if the code was working and have a look at the results in each step, so
troubleshooting was easier. And once we were sure that everything was ok with
the code and the results, we transformed it into a loop to test all comparisons.

NOTE: Since the SYMBOL annotation that will be used in the next analysis comes
from the "palmieri_final" object, which has already been filtered for unique
mapping, no re-annotation is needed in further steps, this also maintains
consistency across the Volcano, GO, and KEGG analysis.

# Volcano Plot Part 1: DEG Parameters - Single comparison
This first part of the volcano plotting manages the differentially expressed
genes identification, meaning we define the parameters that select the DEG in
each comparison, and as a result we get a ".csv" file with the list of DEGs
for each analyzed comparison, which is the same list we later use for the
functional analysis (GO and KEGG analysis), and once all data is collected we
use it for part 2 of the volcano plotting.
```{r Volcano Plot.p1: DEG Parameters - Single}

# Select one comparison to test
tissue_test <- "G"   #"B", "L", or "G"
comp_test   <- "G_T2_IMvsEM"  #The name here must match the names on the tables list
table_test <- tables[[tissue_test]][[comp_test]]

# Print which comparison is being tested
cat("Running Volcano for:", comp_test, "in", tissue_test, "\n")

# Store skip messages
skip_messages <- c()

# 1. Tissue-specific universe
gene_IDs <- backgrounds[[tissue_test]]

# 2. Define and classify DEGs
tab <- table_test

tab$diffexpressed <- "NO"
tab$diffexpressed[tab$logFC >=  2 & tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05] <- "UP"
tab$diffexpressed[tab$logFC <= -2 & tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05] <- "DOWN"

# Extract DEG probe IDs
UP_genes   <- rownames(tab)[tab$diffexpressed == "UP"]
DOWN_genes <- rownames(tab)[tab$diffexpressed == "DOWN"]

# Capture number of DEGs
n_UP_DEG   <- length(UP_genes)
n_DOWN_DEG <- length(DOWN_genes)

# Summary table
summary_table_volcano <- data.frame(
  Comparison = paste(tissue_test, comp_test, sep="_"),
  Tissue = tissue_test,
  Direction = c("UP","DOWN"),
  Universe_size = length(gene_IDs),
  DEGs = c(n_UP_DEG, n_DOWN_DEG),
  Valid_Probes = 0,
  SYMBOLs = 0
)

# Safety check — no DEGs
if(n_UP_DEG == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No UP DEGs")
}

if(n_DOWN_DEG == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DOWN DEGs")
}

if(n_UP_DEG == 0 & n_DOWN_DEG == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DEGs")
  stop("No DEGs detected")
}


# 3. Keep only valid probes
valid_probes <- keys(salmontranscriptcluster.db, "PROBEID")

# Capture number of valid probes
UP_genes   <- intersect(UP_genes, valid_probes)
DOWN_genes <- intersect(DOWN_genes, valid_probes)

# Update summary table with valid DEGs
summary_table_volcano$Valid_Probes[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="UP"] <- length(UP_genes)
summary_table_volcano$Valid_Probes[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="DOWN"] <- length(DOWN_genes)

# Safety check — no valid probes
if(length(UP_genes) == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No UP valid probes")
}

if(length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DOWN valid probes")
}

if(length(UP_genes) == 0 & length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No valid probes")
  stop("No valid probes detected")
}


# 4. Count SYMBOLs directly from table_test
# Count unique symbols among DEGs (only valid probes)
UP_symbols <- unique(na.omit(tab$SYMBOL[rownames(tab) %in% UP_genes]))
DOWN_symbols <- unique(na.omit(tab$SYMBOL[rownames(tab) %in% DOWN_genes]))

# Capture unique symbols
n_UP_symbol <- length(UP_symbols)
n_DOWN_symbol <- length(DOWN_symbols)

# Update summary table with number of SYMBOLS
summary_table_volcano$SYMBOLs[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="UP"] <- n_UP_symbol
summary_table_volcano$SYMBOLs[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="DOWN"] <- n_DOWN_symbol


# 5. Create DEG table
deg_table <- tab[tab$diffexpressed != "NO", ]

# Order data
deg_table <- deg_table[
  order(
    deg_table$diffexpressed, # Order alphabetically
    deg_table$adj.P.Val,     # Then: smallest FDR first
    -abs(deg_table$logFC)    # Then: largest effect size first
  ),
]

# Save DEG CSV
write.csv(deg_table,
          file = paste0("DEG_", tissue_test, "_", comp_test, ".csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)


# HERE WE PAUSE THE ANALYSIS, and continue at the next VolcanoPlot chunk/section

# 8. Save summary + debug
# Save summary CSV
write.csv(summary_table_volcano,
            file = "Volcano_summary_single.csv",
            sep = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = !file.exists("Volcano_summary_single.csv"),
            append = TRUE)

# Create debug table
volcano_log_single <- data.frame(
  comparison = paste(tissue_test, comp_test, sep="_"),
  skipped = length(skip_messages) > 0,
  reason = ifelse(length(skip_messages) > 0,
                  paste(skip_messages, collapse = " | "),
                  NA)
)

# Save debug CSV
write.csv(volcano_log_single,
          file = "Volcano_debug_single.csv",
            sep = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = !file.exists("Volcano_debug_single.csv"),
            append = TRUE)
```


# Volcano Plot Part 1: DEG Parameters - Loop over all comparisons
Here we repeat the volcano analysis in a loop that processes all comparisons.
```{r Volcano Plot.p1: DEG Parameters - Loop}

# A reusable volcano function
make_volcano <- function(tab, comparison_name, tissue, backgrounds, db_object) {
    
    # Print to see which comparison is being processed
    cat("Running Volcano for:", comparison_name, "in", tissue, "\n")
  
    # Store skip messages
    skip_messages <- c()
    
    # 1. Tissue-specific universe
    gene_IDs <- backgrounds[[tissue]]
    
    # 2. Define and classify DEGs
    tab$diffexpressed <- "NO"
    tab$diffexpressed[tab$logFC >=  2 & tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05] <- "UP"
    tab$diffexpressed[tab$logFC <= -2 & tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05] <- "DOWN"
    
    # Extract DEG probe IDs
    UP_genes   <- rownames(tab)[tab$diffexpressed == "UP"]
    DOWN_genes <- rownames(tab)[tab$diffexpressed == "DOWN"]
    
    # Capture number of DEG
    n_UP_DEG   <- length(UP_genes)
    n_DOWN_DEG <- length(DOWN_genes)
    
    # Summary table
    summary_table_volcano <- data.frame(
      Comparison = comparison_name,
      Tissue = tissue,
      Direction = c("UP","DOWN"),
      Universe_size = length(gene_IDs),
      DEGs = c(n_UP_DEG, n_DOWN_DEG),
      Valid_Probes = 0,
      SYMBOLs = 0
      )  
    
    # Safety check — no DEGs
    if(n_UP_DEG == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No UP DEGs")
      }

    if(n_DOWN_DEG == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DOWN DEGs")
      }

    if(n_UP_DEG == 0 & n_DOWN_DEG == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DEGs")
      return(list(
        summary = summary_table_volcano,
        skipped = TRUE,
        reason = paste(skip_messages, collapse = " | ")
      ))
      }

    
    # 3. Keep only valid probes
    valid_probes <- keys(db_object, "PROBEID")

    # Intersect DEGs with valid probes
    UP_genes   <- intersect(UP_genes, valid_probes)
    DOWN_genes <- intersect(DOWN_genes, valid_probes)

    # Update summary table with valid DEGs
    summary_table_volcano$Valid_Probes[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="UP"] <- length(UP_genes)
    summary_table_volcano$Valid_Probes[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="DOWN"] <- length(DOWN_genes)
    
  
    # Safety check — no valid probes
    if(length(UP_genes) == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No UP valid probes")
      }

    if(length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No DOWN valid probes")
      }

    if(length(UP_genes) == 0 & length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
      skip_messages <- c(skip_messages, "No valid probes")
      return(list(
        summary = summary_table_volcano,
        skipped = TRUE,
        reason = "No valid probes"
      ))
      }

    
    # 4. Count SYMBOLs directly from tab
    # Count unique symbols among DEGs (only valid probes)
    UP_symbols <- unique(na.omit(tab$SYMBOL[rownames(tab) %in% UP_genes]))
    DOWN_symbols <- unique(na.omit(tab$SYMBOL[rownames(tab) %in% DOWN_genes]))

    # Capture unique symbols
    n_UP_symbol <- length(UP_symbols)
    n_DOWN_symbol <- length(DOWN_symbols)

    # Update summary table with number of SYMBOLS
    summary_table_volcano$SYMBOLs[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="UP"] <- n_UP_symbol
    summary_table_volcano$SYMBOLs[summary_table_volcano$Direction=="DOWN"] <- n_DOWN_symbol

    # 5. Create DEGs table for CSV
    deg_table <- tab[tab$diffexpressed != "NO", ]
    
    # Order data
    deg_table <- deg_table[
      order(
        deg_table$diffexpressed, # Order alphabetically
        deg_table$adj.P.Val,     # Then: smallest FDR first
        -abs(deg_table$logFC)    # Then: largest effect size first
        ),
      ]
   
    
# HERE WE PAUSE THE ANALYSIS, and continue at the next VolcanoPlot chunk/section

    
    # Save CSV with DEGs
    write.csv(deg_table,
            file = paste0("DEG_", comparison_name, ".csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
    
    return(list(
      summary = summary_table_volcano,
      skipped = FALSE,
      reason = ifelse(length(skip_messages)>0,
                      paste(skip_messages, collapse=" | "),
                      NA)
    ))
}


# Loop over ALL tissues and all comparisons
volcano_results_all <- list()

for (tissue in names(tables)) {
  for (comp in names(tables[[tissue]])) {

    result <- make_volcano(
      tab = tables[[tissue]][[comp]],
      comparison_name = paste(tissue, comp, sep="_"),
      tissue = tissue,
      backgrounds = backgrounds,
      db_object = salmontranscriptcluster.db
    )

    volcano_results_all[[paste(tissue, comp, sep="_")]] <- result
  }
}


# AFTER loop → create debug table
volcano_log <- data.frame(
  comparison = names(volcano_results_all),
  skipped = sapply(volcano_results_all, function(x) x$skipped),
  reason  = sapply(volcano_results_all, function(x) x$reason)
)

# Save debug table as CSV
write.csv(volcano_log, "Volcano_debug_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)


# AFTER loop  → create MASTER summary table
all_summary_volcano <- do.call(rbind,
  lapply(volcano_results_all, function(x) x$summary)
)

# Save master summary as CSV
write.csv(all_summary_volcano,
          file = "Volcano_summary_AllComparisons.csv",
          sep = ",",
          row.names = FALSE,
          col.names = TRUE,  # Always write headers for master
          append = FALSE)    # Fresh file, not appending
```



# Functional Annotation Analysis
For the functional analysis of our DEG we will perform both GO and KEGG analysis.

## Gene ontology (GO) based enrichment analysis - Single comparison
GO enrichment was also done per tissue, per contrast, and performed using the
"topGO" function from the package of the same name, with the "elim" algorithm
and Fisher’s exact statistical test.
```{r Functional Analysis: GO - Single}

# Choose a comparison
comparison_name <- "G5_T1_IMvsEM"

# Define UP and DOWN gene sets
UP_genes   <- rownames(table_g5)[table_g5$logFC >=  2 & table_g5$adj.P.Val < 0.05]
DOWN_genes <- rownames(table_g5)[table_g5$logFC <= -2 & table_g5$adj.P.Val < 0.05]

# Store number of DEGs for CSV
n_UP_DEG   <- length(UP_genes)
n_DOWN_DEG <- length(DOWN_genes)

# Safety check 1 — No DEGs
if(length(UP_genes) == 0){
  message("No UP DEGs detected")
}

if(length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  message("No DOWN DEGs detected")
}

if(length(UP_genes) == 0 & length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  message("Skipping GO analysis: no DEGs")
  return(NULL)
}

# Filter to keep only probes that are on the DB
valid_probes <- keys(salmontranscriptcluster.db, "PROBEID")

# Intersect objects to keep only valid probes
UP_genes <- intersect(UP_genes, valid_probes)
DOWN_genes <- intersect(DOWN_genes, valid_probes)

# Capture valid probes to save later in CSV
n_UP_valid   <- length(UP_genes)
n_DOWN_valid <- length(DOWN_genes)

# Safety check 2 — No valid probes in DB
if(length(UP_genes) == 0){
  message("No UP genes with valid PROBEID")
}

if(length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  message("No DOWN genes with valid PROBEID")
}


# Gene universe: Tissue-specific - change according to the tested comparison
gene_IDs <- gonad_bg$probes

# Extract probe → GO term mapping from salmon DB
gene2go <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  salmontranscriptcluster.db,
  keys     = gene_IDs,
  keytype  = "PROBEID",
  columns  = "GO"
)

# Remove NAs and split into 2 columns
gene2go <- gene2go[!is.na(gene2go$GO), ]
gene2GO_list <- split(gene2go$GO, gene2go$PROBEID)

# Store probes, from the universe, with GO annotation
mapped_probes <- unique(gene2go$PROBEID)

# Track DE-valid probes entering GO analysis
UP_genes <- intersect(UP_genes, mapped_probes)
DOWN_genes <- intersect(DOWN_genes, mapped_probes)

# Capture valid probes with GO annotation, to save later in CSV
n_UP_GO   <- length(UP_genes)
n_DOWN_GO <- length(DOWN_genes)

# Safety check 3 — No DEGs with GO terms
if(length(UP_genes) == 0){
  message("Skipping UP GO: no genes with GO annotations")
}

if(length(DOWN_genes) == 0){
  message("Skipping DOWN GO: no genes with GO annotations")
}


# Extract probe → gene mapping from salmon DB
probe2gene_table <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  salmontranscriptcluster.db,
  keys = gene_IDs,
  keytype = "PROBEID",
  columns = "SYMBOL"
)

# Remove probes without gene names
probe2gene_table <- probe2gene_table[!is.na(probe2gene_table$SYMBOL), ]

# Convert it into a mapping vector
probe2gene <- setNames(probe2gene_table$SYMBOL, probe2gene_table$PROBEID)
probe2gene[1]


# Create two gene vectors
all_genes_up <- factor(as.integer(gene_IDs %in% UP_genes, levels = c(0,1)))
names(all_genes_up) <- gene_IDs

all_genes_down <- factor(as.integer(gene_IDs %in% DOWN_genes, levels = c(0,1)))
names(all_genes_down) <- gene_IDs

# Create two topGO objects with safety check 4
top_GO_up <- NULL
if(length(UP_genes) > 0){
top_GO_up <- new(
  "topGOdata",
  ontology = "BP",
  allGenes = all_genes_up,
  gene2GO  = gene2GO_list,
  nodeSize = 10,
  annot    = annFUN.gene2GO
)
}

top_GO_down <- NULL
if(length(DOWN_genes) > 0){
top_GO_down <- new(
  "topGOdata",
  ontology = "BP",
  allGenes = all_genes_down,
  gene2GO  = gene2GO_list,
  nodeSize = 10,
  annot    = annFUN.gene2GO
)
}

# Initialize result objects (prevents environment contamination)
res_up_topGO <- NULL
res_down_topGO <- NULL

# Now the tests can be run for UP genes with safety check 5
result_up_topGO_elim <- NULL
if(!is.null(top_GO_up)){
result_up_topGO_elim <- 
  runTest(top_GO_up, algorithm = "elim", statistic = "Fisher")
}

# We extract results in data frame for UP genes with safety check 6
if(!is.null(result_up_topGO_elim)){
res_up_topGO <- GenTable(top_GO_up, Fisher.elim = result_up_topGO_elim,
        orderBy = "Fisher.elim", topNodes = length(score(result_up_topGO_elim)))
}
head(res_up_topGO)

# Convert p-values to numeric, topGO stores them as strings, for UP genes
res_up_topGO$Fisher.elim <- as.numeric(res_up_topGO$Fisher.elim)
head(res_up_topGO)

# Remove NAs in Fisher.elim column
res_up_topGO <- res_up_topGO[!is.na(res_up_topGO$Fisher.elim), ]

# Now the tests can be run for DOWN genes  with safety check 5
result_down_topGO_elim <- NULL
if(!is.null(top_GO_down)){
result_down_topGO_elim <- 
  runTest(top_GO_down, algorithm = "elim", statistic = "Fisher")
}

# We extract results in data frame for DOWN genes with safety check 6
if(!is.null(result_down_topGO_elim)){
res_down_topGO <- GenTable(top_GO_down, Fisher.elim = result_down_topGO_elim,
        orderBy = "Fisher.elim",
        topNodes = length(score(result_down_topGO_elim)))
}
head(res_down_topGO)

# Convert p-values to numeric, topGO stores them as strings, for DOWN genes
res_down_topGO$Fisher.elim <- as.numeric(res_down_topGO$Fisher.elim)
head(res_down_topGO)

# Remove NAs in Fisher.elim column
res_down_topGO <- res_down_topGO[!is.na(res_down_topGO$Fisher.elim), ]

# Capture number of GO terms obtained after analysis
n_UP_GO_terms   <- if(!is.null(res_up_topGO)) nrow(res_up_topGO) else 0
n_DOWN_GO_terms <- if(!is.null(res_down_topGO)) nrow(res_down_topGO) else 0

cat("UP GO terms:", n_UP_GO_terms, "\n")
cat("DOWN GO terms:", n_DOWN_GO_terms, "\n")

# Capture significant GO terms obtained after analysis
n_UP_GO_sig <- if(!is.null(res_up_topGO))
  sum(res_up_topGO$Fisher.elim < 0.05) else 0

n_DOWN_GO_sig <- if(!is.null(res_down_topGO))
  sum(res_down_topGO$Fisher.elim < 0.05) else 0

# To extract probes list
# Extract GO -> probes mappings from topGO objects
# This function from topGO retrieves a list of the internal mapping
GO2probe_up <- NULL
if(!is.null(top_GO_up)){
GO2probe_up <- genesInTerm(top_GO_up)
}

GO2probe_down <- NULL
if(!is.null(top_GO_down)){
GO2probe_down <- genesInTerm(top_GO_down)
}

# Function to extract probes for each GO term
extract_probes <- function(go_ids, GO2probe, DEG_list){
  sapply(go_ids, function(go){
    probes <- GO2probe[[go]]
    
    # If GO term not found return NA
    if(is.null(probes)) return(NA)
    
    # Keep only DE genes belonging to the term
    probes <- probes[probes %in% DEG_list]
    
    if(length(probes) == 0) return(NA)
    paste(probes, collapse = ",")
  })
}

# Get probe lists for UP and DOWN tables
if(!is.null(res_up_topGO)){
res_up_topGO$Probes <- extract_probes(
  res_up_topGO$GO.ID,
  GO2probe_up,
  UP_genes
)
}

if(!is.null(res_down_topGO)){
res_down_topGO$Probes <- extract_probes(
  res_down_topGO$GO.ID,
  GO2probe_down,
  DOWN_genes
)
}

# Combine UP + DOWN and add direction to GO results with safety check 7
go_list <- list()
if(!is.null(res_up_topGO) && is.data.frame(res_up_topGO) && nrow(res_up_topGO) > 0){
  res_up_topGO$Direction <- "UP"
  go_list[["UP"]] <- res_up_topGO
}

if(!is.null(res_down_topGO) && is.data.frame(res_down_topGO) && nrow(res_down_topGO) > 0){
  res_down_topGO$Direction <- "DOWN"
  go_list[["DOWN"]] <- res_down_topGO
}

# If no GO term results at all
if(length(go_list) == 0){
  message("No GO enrichment results")
  return(NULL)
}

# Combine
go_all <- do.call(rbind, go_list)


# Function to convert GO terms probe lists into gene names
convert_probes_to_genes <- function(probe_string, mapping){

  if(is.na(probe_string)) return(NA)
  probes <- unlist(strsplit(probe_string, ","))
  genes <- mapping[probes]
  genes <- unique(genes)
  genes <- genes[!is.na(genes)]
  paste(genes, collapse = ",")
}

# Apply to GO results
go_all$GeneSymbols <- sapply(go_all$Probes, convert_probes_to_genes, probe2gene)

# Count all recovered symbols
n_UP_symbol <- length(unique(
  na.omit(unlist(strsplit(
    go_all$GeneSymbols[go_all$Direction == "UP"], ","
  )))
))

n_DOWN_symbol <- length(unique(
  na.omit(unlist(strsplit(
    go_all$GeneSymbols[go_all$Direction == "DOWN"], ","
  )))
))


# Calculate -log10Pvalue
go_all$logPvalue <- -log10(go_all$Fisher.elim)

# Separate significant GO terms
go_sig <- go_all[go_all$Fisher.elim < 0.05, ]

# Count symbols from significant GO terms
n_UP_symbol_sig <- length(unique(
  na.omit(unlist(strsplit(
    go_sig$GeneSymbols[go_sig$Direction == "UP"], ","
  )))
))

n_DOWN_symbol_sig <- length(unique(
  na.omit(unlist(strsplit(
    go_sig$GeneSymbols[go_sig$Direction == "DOWN"], ","
  )))
))


# Build summary table
summary_table_GO <- data.frame(
  Comparison = rep(comparison_name,2),
  Direction = c("UP","DOWN"),
  Universe_size = length(gene_IDs),
  
  DEGs = c(n_UP_DEG, n_DOWN_DEG),
  Probes_entering_GOmapping = c(n_UP_valid, n_DOWN_valid),
  Probes_entering_GOenrich = c(n_UP_GO, n_DOWN_GO),
  GO_terms = c(n_UP_GO_terms, n_DOWN_GO_terms),
  SYMBOLs_from_GOterms = c(n_UP_symbol, n_DOWN_symbol),
  GO_signif = c(n_UP_GO_sig, n_DOWN_GO_sig),
  SYMBOLs_from_signifGO = c(n_UP_symbol_sig, n_DOWN_symbol_sig)
  )


# Save summary table, per each comparison tested, in a master CSV
write.csv(summary_table_GO,
            file = "7mayGO_summary_AllComparisons.csv",
            sep = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = !file.exists("7mayGO_summary_AllComparisons.csv"),
            append = TRUE)


# Save topGO results for UP&DOWN genes as CSV
write.csv(go_all,
          file = "GO_UP_DOWN_G_T1_IMvsEM.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)


# Filter significant GO terms and show top 15
go_plot <- go_all %>%
  group_by(Direction) %>%
  filter(Fisher.elim < 0.05) %>%        # keep only significant terms
  arrange(Fisher.elim, .by_group = TRUE) %>%  # order by smallest p-value
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%                # keep max 15 per group
  ungroup()

# Make sure GO terms are factors to control the order in the plot
go_plot$Term <- factor(go_plot$Term, levels = rev(unique(go_plot$Term)))


# Faceted dotplot (UP vs DOWN)
if(nrow(go_plot) > 0){

p <- ggplot(go_plot, aes(x = logPvalue, 
                   y = Term,
                   color = Direction,
                   size = Significant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~Direction, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = "steelblue3", "UP" = "firebrick3")) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 10), breaks = sort(unique(go_plot$Significant))) +  # adjust bubble sizes and only signif.numbers in legend
  labs(
    x = "-log10(p-value)",
    y = "GO Term",
    size = "Gene Count",
    color = "Direction"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15), #bigger axis letters
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14), #bigger axis numbers
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18), #bold axis labels
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),  # facet labels
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),   # bold legend titles
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

tiff("GO_UP_DOWN_dotplot.tiff", width = 17, height = 12, units = "in", res = 600)

print(p)

dev.off()
} else {
message("No significant GO terms to plot")
}
```
